summary.oneLiner: One of India's leading textile manufacturers, producing cotton/polyester-cotton blended and synthetic yarns for the weaving and knitting industries in India and over 30 countries.
summary.business: Incorporated in 1989, Sportking India Limited manufactures a well-diversified range of grey and dyed textile yarns (cotton/polyester-cotton blended and synthetic yarns) to meet the requirements of the weaving and knitting industries. The Company operates three manufacturing facilities in India equipped with modern machinery and serves both domestic (Pan-India) and international markets, exporting to 36 countries with exports contributing around 51% of total turnover.

currentContext.strategies: The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy is founded on trusteeship, empowerment, accountability, control and ethical practices with transparency, and holds that driving growth creates maximum shareholder value. The stated objective is to reward shareholders by sharing a portion of profits while retaining sufficient funds for future growth, maintaining a consistent approach to dividend pay-out over time; the policy applies to both interim and final dividends and excludes preference-share dividends, dividend-in-kind (bonus shares/other securities) and cash distribution via buyback. For FY2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 1.00 per equity share of face value Rs. 1.00 each, to be paid out of the Company's profits.
currentContext.expansion: The Company is executing a greenfield expansion project to add 150,000 (One Lakh Fifty Thousand) spindles of spinning capacity. Financial closure for the project has been completed; land has been secured, requisite approvals obtained, and advances for machinery made. Building and construction work is at an advanced stage, and the project is expected to commence before the end of the current fiscal year (FY2026-27), aimed at meeting growing product demand, improving operational efficiency and generating business synergies through modernisation. Separately, the Company acquired a 26% equity stake (Rs. 14.10 crore) in Evincea Renewable Seven Private Limited, a Special Purpose Vehicle developing a 40.3 MW captive solar power project to supply solar energy to the Company's Punjab facilities under a 25-year Solar Power Purchase Agreement; the project commenced commercial operations on 18th June 2026 and is expected to reduce annual power costs by approximately 12-13%.
currentContext.mdna: Government temporarily exempted basic customs duty on raw cotton imports (June-October 2026), aimed at improving raw cotton availability and stabilizing input costs for yarn manufacturers.|RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) scheme extended up to September 30, 2026, ensuring continuity of export incentives for textile exporters.|Government allocated approximately Rs. 5,252 crore to the Ministry of Textiles in FY2025-26; PLI Scheme, PM MITRA Mega Textile Parks and the National Technical Textiles Mission continue to support capacity expansion and value-added manufacturing across the sector.|Global sourcing diversification under the 'China+1' strategy is strengthening India's (and peers Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Turkey) position as a preferred textile sourcing destination.|India's textile and apparel exports (including handicrafts) grew around 2.1% over FY2024-25, led by Ready-Made Garments, followed by cotton yarn, fabrics, made-ups and handloom products.|Indian textile exports were impacted early in FY2025-26 by higher U.S. tariff-related uncertainties and reciprocal duties, causing order delays, pricing pressure and cautious buying by global retailers, before easing trade tensions supported a recovery in export sentiment later in the year.|Textile yarn industry demand and margins remain exposed to raw material (cotton) price volatility driven by monsoon performance, temperature variations and pest incidence, which can create a mismatch between input costs and yarn realizations.|Industry exposed to global demand cycles centered on the United States and Europe, with economic slowdown, inflation, and geopolitical/tariff developments able to reduce demand and disrupt sourcing decisions.|Medium- to long-term Indian textile industry outlook remains positive, supported by domestic consumption, supply-chain diversification, PLI schemes, export incentives, FTAs and infrastructure expansion, though short-term volatility from global uncertainties persists.

risks.risk: Raw material (cotton/fibre) price and availability volatility
risks.note: Cotton production and quality are influenced by monsoon performance, temperature variations and pest incidence; resulting price volatility directly affects procurement costs, particularly when yarn realizations do not adjust in line with input cost movements, creating uncertainty in planning and margin stability.

The industry (and Company) depends on key export markets such as the United States and Europe; economic slowdown, inflationary pressures, shifting consumer preferences, geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and tariff-related developments can disrupt supply chains and reduce demand, while rising competition from other producing countries intensifies pricing pressure.

Being export-oriented, the industry is exposed to INR/USD fluctuations that can affect revenue realization and margins; liquidity constraints, interest-rate fluctuations, delayed receivables and tightening credit conditions from domestic and international buyers can also impact working-capital cycles.

risks.risk: Rising energy, fuel and logistics costs
risks.note: Increasing input costs add pressure on operating margins, especially for manufacturing units with limited ability to pass through costs to customers.

Growing use of digital systems in manufacturing, finance and supply-chain management increases exposure to data breaches, ransomware attacks and system disruptions that can affect operational continuity and data integrity.

Stricter ESG norms on emissions, water usage and waste management may require additional investment in sustainable technologies, increasing short-term operating costs for the industry and the Company.

thesis (one-line): Best cotton-yarn spreads in ~3 years (>$1/kg vs $0.65–0.70 normal) + China demand resurgence + rupee tailwind + a ~INR1,000 cr / 150k-spindle greenfield (commercial ops Q3 FY27) set up margin expansion and volume growth into FY27, with forward integration (Marvel/Sobhagia) as a longer-term value-added optionality.
scorecard (yoy / qoq where stated; value:
| Metric | Read | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | "broadly stable" / "resilient" in Q4; profitability improved | No absolute Q4 figure given on call. FY27 guided top line ~INR2,700–2,800 cr (incl. ~INR200 cr from new acquisitions). |
| EBITDA margin | **~13% in Q4 FY26** | Mgmt: "could have been higher but we have some small provisions." Expansion expected next 2–3 quarters. |
| PAT (reported) | Improved YoY; congratulated as "record set of numbers" | Dampened by a **forex MTM hit** — USD closed at all-time high on 31-Mar; unshipped/unreceived export booked MTM. |
| PAT (normalized) | Higher ex-forex MTM | MTM is notional, expected to reverse in Q1 FY27 if rupee doesn't depreciate further. |
| **VOLUME** | At **full / optimum capacity ~95–96%** | No volume growth expected for next ~3 quarters until new greenfield ramps (Q3/Q4 FY27). |
| **Cotton-yarn spread** ⭐ | **>$1/kg** between skein cost & final yarn price (3-year high, "expanding") | Vs ~$0.65–0.70 for prior couple of years. Yarn realization risen from ~USD2.70–2.80/kg last qtr to ~USD3.30/kg now. |
| Export mix ⭐ | **~50% (±5%)** international, stable for years | Bangladesh = #1 export market; China raised from ~2–3% to ~10–12% of Sportking exports in last quarter. |
| Net debt | Not disclosed on call | INR1,000 cr greenfield underway; machinery advances released. |

> CALL OUT: Cotton-yarn spread >$1/kg (3-yr high, expanding) and export mix ~50% with China rising to 10–12% of Sportking's exports are the two load-bearing numbers.
guidance (critical — explicit):
- **Volume:** Flat near term (already at ~95–96% optimum utilization). New greenfield production "a little bit" in Q3 FY27, more substantial Q4 FY27, full from FY28.
- **Top line:** +7–10% over next 3 quarters driven by **higher yarn prices** (not volume). FY27 (coming FY) top line guided ~INR2,700–2,800 cr.
- **Spread:** Confident spreads hold/improve for next 2–3 quarters — 90-day export sales book already covers ~this quarter + next half-quarter sold; cotton covered for 3–6 months.
- **Margins:** Expect QoQ margin expansion "by at least 15%, 20%" over next 2–3 quarters. On H1 FY27 >15% EBITDA margin: "I'll be disappointed if we don't." Long-term sustainable industry margin pegged ~15%.
- **Capacity expansion:** Greenfield ~150,000 spindles (~40% of current capacity, Phase 1), ~INR1,000 cr; commercial ops Q3 FY27; full utilization (97–98%) ~6 months post-commissioning, ramping ~15–16%/month.
- **Value-added mix:** Forward integration (Marvel dyeing/processing; Sobhagia fabric/garments) — integration over next 12–18 months; bigger downstream plans deferred ~6–9 months / 1 year. Acquisitions add ~INR200 cr top line (7–8% of turnover); minimal near-term margin impact.
demand:
- Broad-based demand recovery across **all geographies and all segments** for last 3–4 months; described as structural, not just cyclical.
- **China resurgence:** China's share of India's yarn imports up from ~7–8% to ~25–30%; India's overall export share ~23–24% over last 4–5 months. Driver: China domestic demand turning corner after 4–5 weak years; China raw-cotton production peaked → needs to import; high cotton import duty (~40%/quotas) makes importing **cotton yarn** an arbitrage.
- **Bangladesh:** Renewed optimism post-elections; still #1 export market though some share ceded to China due to production constraints.
- **Domestic:** Lagged early but "leading the charge" since March after US tariff went away.
segment color (cotton / blended / melang: - Demand strong "across all the segments that we meet" and "all kinds of yarns — not only cotton yarn." Cotton yarn explicitly called out as primary spread/realization driver. No segment-wise revenue split disclosed on call.
growth / optionality:
- **Greenfield:** ~150k spindles, ~INR1,000 cr, Odisha; commercial Q3 FY27; ~40% capacity add (Phase 1), more phases to follow.
- **Forward integration:** Marvel Dyers & Processors (majority stake; dyeing/processing) + Sobhagia Sales (slump-sale mfg facilities; fabric/garments). Positioned as "labs for future downstream expansions"; revenue scale-up: group cos FY27 +15–20%.
- **FTAs:** EU & UK FTAs — UK expected active in 2–3 months, EU ~6 months; both effective by end-FY27. Seen as next-year stimulus when new capacity comes online.
- **India-as-hub:** Mgmt sees India becoming garment/fabric hub substituting China (stable power/policy/rates); "any meaningful increase in demand can really jack up the spreads."
margins & cost (cotton, power):
- Q4 EBITDA margin ~13%, held back by "small provisions." Margin driver = better spreads, robust demand.
- **Cotton:** Covered for 3–6 months / by end-March (annual practice for quality). Indian cotton currently substantially cheaper than international, regained competitiveness after intl rally + rupee softening.
- **Power/Solar:** 40 MW solar to commence end-May; ~7 cr units/yr at INR3.70/unit; saving ~INR14–15 cr/yr (~INR2/unit). Max permissible under Punjab policy for existing capacity. Odisha gets cheap solar already → only small rooftop there, no ground solar.
capex:
- Greenfield ~INR1,000 cr (land acquired, machinery advances released, construction on schedule; commercial Q3 FY27).
- 40 MW solar (commencing end-May FY27).
- Acquisitions: Marvel + Sobhagia (amounts not disclosed; ~INR200 cr combined revenue).
capital allocation: - Heavy organic capex (greenfield) + bolt-on downstream acquisitions for integration; solar for cost saving. No buyback/dividend commentary on call. Cotton inventory funded via annual full-season coverage.
risks:
- **Cotton import duty** — "big thorn in the flesh"; not biting now (Indian cotton cheaper) but long-term detriment; lobbying ministries, resolution awaited.
- **CCI buying behavior** — CCI bought ~106 lakh bales of ~310 lakh projected (~33–34%); raises market prices toward MSP Oct–Feb when mills must buy → cost pressure.
- **China demand volatility** — historically volatile partner; mgmt circumspect on increasing share despite optimism.
- **New cotton crop / price risk** — if next India crop lower, procurement cost up → spread compression beyond Q2.
- **Forex MTM** — quarter-end USD spikes create notional swings (Q4 hit, reversible).
- **Macro** — multiple wars, higher-inflation forecasts, seasonally weak Apr–Sep spinning quarters.
management tone: - Confident, candid; "more excited about the long-term future." Sticks to guidance discipline ("we don't give guidance, but I'll be disappointed if we don't" do 15%+). Stresses consolidation thesis ("modernize or shut down") favoring efficient large players like Sportking.
non-obvious points:
- China importing **cotton yarn** (not raw cotton) is an *arbitrage* play around China's ~40% cotton-import duty + peaked domestic cotton production — a structurally stickier driver than past spikes.
- Spread improvement from ~$0.65–0.70 → >$1/kg is the real earnings lever; revenue "stable" understates profit leverage.
- Forex MTM is purely quarter-end-rate mechanical (sell-and-book-same-day policy → no carried FX risk); the Q4 drag should reverse.
- Greenfield in **Odisha** (not Punjab) — gets cheap grid solar, so no ground-solar capex needed there.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ Spinning consolidation (obsolete/unorganized capacity shutting down) → efficient large modern spinners (Sportking) gain share.
- ⭐ EU/UK FTAs + China+1 → Indian yarn/fabric/garment chain; downstream "pulling up socks," capacities coming up in anticipation.
- ⭐ Rupee depreciation → Indian spinning export competitiveness.

---
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** EBITDA margin ~13% (small provisions); revenue stable, profit up; cotton-yarn spread >$1/kg (3-yr high, expanding) vs $0.65–0.70 prior; yarn realization ~USD2.70–2.80 → ~USD3.30/kg; utilization ~95–96% (full); export mix ~50%, China up to 10–12% of Sportking exports; forex MTM drag (USD all-time-high 31-Mar close). Guidance: top line +7–10% over 3 qtrs on price; margins QoQ +15–20%; H1 FY27 >15% EBITDA. Greenfield 150k spindles / ~INR1,000 cr → commercial Q3 FY27. 40 MW solar end-May (~INR14–15 cr/yr saving). Board approved Marvel Dyers (majority stake) + Sobhagia Sales (slump sale) — ~INR200 cr combined revenue, forward integration into dyeing/fabric/garments.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Government temporarily exempted basic customs duty on raw cotton imports (June-October 2026), aimed at improving raw cotton availability and stabilizing input costs for yarn manufacturers.
- RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) scheme extended up to September 30, 2026, ensuring continuity of export incentives for textile exporters.
- Government allocated approximately Rs. 5,252 crore to the Ministry of Textiles in FY2025-26; PLI Scheme, PM MITRA Mega Textile Parks and the National Technical Textiles Mission continue to support capacity expansion and value-added manufacturing across the sector.
- Global sourcing diversification under the 'China+1' strategy is strengthening India's (and peers Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Turkey) position as a preferred textile sourcing destination.
- India's textile and apparel exports (including handicrafts) grew around 2.1% over FY2024-25, led by Ready-Made Garments, followed by cotton yarn, fabrics, made-ups and handloom products.
- Indian textile exports were impacted early in FY2025-26 by higher U.S. tariff-related uncertainties and reciprocal duties, causing order delays, pricing pressure and cautious buying by global retailers, before easing trade tensions supported a recovery in export sentiment later in the year.
- Textile yarn industry demand and margins remain exposed to raw material (cotton) price volatility driven by monsoon performance, temperature variations and pest incidence, which can create a mismatch between input costs and yarn realizations.
- Industry exposed to global demand cycles centered on the United States and Europe, with economic slowdown, inflation, and geopolitical/tariff developments able to reduce demand and disrupt sourcing decisions.
- Medium- to long-term Indian textile industry outlook remains positive, supported by domestic consumption, supply-chain diversification, PLI schemes, export incentives, FTAs and infrastructure expansion, though short-term volatility from global uncertainties persists.

margins.title: Margins & cost (cotton, power)
margins.body:
- Q4 EBITDA margin ~13%, held back by "small provisions." Margin driver = better spreads, robust demand.
- **Cotton:** Covered for 3–6 months / by end-March (annual practice for quality). Indian cotton currently substantially cheaper than international, regained competitiveness after intl rally + rupee softening.
- **Power/Solar:** 40 MW solar to commence end-May; ~7 cr units/yr at INR3.70/unit; saving ~INR14–15 cr/yr (~INR2/unit). Max permissible under Punjab policy for existing capacity. Odisha gets cheap solar already → only small rooftop there, no ground solar.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - Heavy organic capex (greenfield) + bolt-on downstream acquisitions for integration; solar for cost saving. No buyback/dividend commentary on call. Cotton inventory funded via annual full-season coverage.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is executing a greenfield expansion project to add 150,000 (One Lakh Fifty Thousand) spindles of spinning capacity. Financial closure for the project has been completed; land has been secured, requisite approvals obtained, and advances for machinery made. Building and construction work is at an advanced stage, and the project is expected to commence before the end of the current fiscal year (FY2026-27), aimed at meeting growing product demand, improving operational efficiency and generating business synergies through modernisation. Separately, the Company acquired a 26% equity stake (Rs. 14.10 crore) in Evincea Renewable Seven Private Limited, a Special Purpose Vehicle developing a 40.3 MW captive solar power project to supply solar energy to the Company's Punjab facilities under a 25-year Solar Power Purchase Agreement; the project commenced commercial operations on 18th June 2026 and is expected to reduce annual power costs by approximately 12-13%.

management_tone.title: Management tone
management_tone.body: - Confident, candid; "more excited about the long-term future." Sticks to guidance discipline ("we don't give guidance, but I'll be disappointed if we don't" do 15%+). Stresses consolidation thesis ("modernize or shut down") favoring efficient large players like Sportking.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified range of grey and dyed textile yarns serving both weaving and knitting industries
- Established international presence with exports to 36 countries contributing around 51% of total turnover
- Three manufacturing facilities equipped with modern/latest machinery producing yarns positioned as a quality benchmark

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- **Cotton import duty** — "big thorn in the flesh"; not biting now (Indian cotton cheaper) but long-term detriment; lobbying ministries, resolution awaited.
- **CCI buying behavior** — CCI bought ~106 lakh bales of ~310 lakh projected (~33–34%); raises market prices toward MSP Oct–Feb when mills must buy → cost pressure.
- **China demand volatility** — historically volatile partner; mgmt circumspect on increasing share despite optimism.
- **New cotton crop / price risk** — if next India crop lower, procurement cost up → spread compression beyond Q2.
- **Forex MTM** — quarter-end USD spikes create notional swings (Q4 hit, reversible).
- **Macro** — multiple wars, higher-inflation forecasts, seasonally weak Apr–Sep spinning quarters.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious points
non_obvious.body:
- China importing **cotton yarn** (not raw cotton) is an *arbitrage* play around China's ~40% cotton-import duty + peaked domestic cotton production — a structurally stickier driver than past spikes.
- Spread improvement from ~$0.65–0.70 → >$1/kg is the real earnings lever; revenue "stable" understates profit leverage.
- Forex MTM is purely quarter-end-rate mechanical (sell-and-book-same-day policy → no carried FX risk); the Q4 drag should reverse.
- Greenfield in **Odisha** (not Punjab) — gets cheap grid solar, so no ground-solar capex needed there.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body: The Company's Dividend Distribution Policy is founded on trusteeship, empowerment, accountability, control and ethical practices with transparency, and holds that driving growth creates maximum shareholder value. The stated objective is to reward shareholders by sharing a portion of profits while retaining sufficient funds for future growth, maintaining a consistent approach to dividend pay-out over time; the policy applies to both interim and final dividends and excludes preference-share dividends, dividend-in-kind (bonus shares/other securities) and cash distribution via buyback. For …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ✅ Spinning consolidation (obsolete/unorganized capacity shutting down) → efficient large modern spinners (Sportking) gain share.
- ⭐ EU/UK FTAs + China+1 → Indian yarn/fabric/garment chain; downstream "pulling up socks," capacities coming up in anticipation.
- ⭐ Rupee depreciation → Indian spinning export competitiveness.

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** EBITDA margin ~13% (small provisions); revenue stable, profit up; cotton-yarn spread >$1/kg (3-yr high, expanding) vs $0.65–0.70 prior; yarn realization ~USD2.70–2.80 → ~USD3.30/kg; utilization ~95–96% (full); export mix ~50%, China up to 10–12% of Sportking exports; forex MTM drag (USD all-time-high 31-Mar close). Guidance: top line +7–10% over 3 qtrs on price; margins QoQ +15–20%; H1 FY27 >15% EBITDA. Greenfield 150k spindles / ~INR1,000 cr → commercial Q3 FY27. 40 MW solar end-May (~INR14–15 cr/yr saving). Board approved Marvel Dyers (majority stake) + Sobhagia Sales (slump sale) — ~INR200 cr combined revenue, forward integration into dyeing/fabric/garments.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [M&A / forward integration] "The Board has approved the acquisition of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors Private Limited, along with the acquisition of manufacturing facilities of Sobhagia Sales Private Limited on a slump sale basis and land and building on lease basis, subject to the completion and execution of definitive agreements." Marvel Dyers does dyeing, printing and finishing of fabrics; Sobhagia Sales manufactures and retails readymade garments.
- [Policy tailwinds] The deck cites a PLI Scheme with a budgetary outlay of Rs 106.83 billion for FY25-26 to FY29-30 for the textile industry (recently extended to medical/hygiene and technical textiles), seven PM-Mitra mega textile parks with capital support of Rs 44.4bn over five years, and a Union Budget 2026-27 allocation of Rs 5,279.01 crore to the Ministry of Textiles (FY26 revised to Rs 5,766.68 crore).
- [Sector outlook, third-party framing] The deck states the textile sector "is expected to breach $100bn by the end of FY30" and flags the China+1 shift plus FTAs signed with the UK, New Zealand and EFTA as export tailwinds - these are industry claims, not company guidance.
- [Governance] Munish Avasthi is Chairman & Managing Director; Chetan Rupal (Whole Time Director) brings "over 15 years of rich experience in the fabric dyeing industry", and Anjali Avasthi (Non-Executive Non-Independent Director) has "over 15 years of experience as a Managing Garments Business" - both skill sets aligned to the proposed fabric and garment acquisitions.
